statement: Let a valid triple (i,j,k) mean 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, 0 <= k, k <= i, i + k < m, k <= j, j + k < n. For a valid triple, let RhombusSum(i,j,k) be the sum of grid[a][b] over all cells (a,b) with 0 <= a < m, 0 <= b < n and |a-i| + |b-j| = k. Let S = { RhombusSum(i,j,k) : (i,j,k) is valid }. Let D = |S|, and list the distinct elements of S in strictly decreasing order as s_1 > s_2 > ... > s_D. The function returns a vector r such that len(r) = min(3,D), and for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), r[t] = s_{t+1}.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The grid is nonempty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= n <= 50, every row of grid has length n, and 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

The function returns a vector r and len(r) = min(3, |S|).
